marble.name: Picture & Bar Graphs
marble.subject: Mathematics
marble.description: Draw a picture graph and a bar graph (with single-unit scale) to represent a data set with up to four categories; solve put-together, take-apart, and compare problems using information presented in a bar graph
marble.prompt: Can you draw a simple bar chart or picture graph to show information — like how many of each colour of sweet are in a bag — and answer questions from it?

cluster.summary: Your child is learning to organise and count information by sorting objects into groups and comparing which groups have more or fewer items.

misconceptions: Answers 'how many more' with the taller bar's value instead of the difference between the bars
Reads a bar's value off by one (counts gridlines instead of the value the top reaches, or bars not starting at zero)
Draws bars of unequal width, floating off the baseline, or unevenly spaced, so height no longer means count
Draws picture-graph symbols of different sizes or unaligned, so rows can't be compared by length
representations: Bar graph with single-unit scale on squared paper
Picture graph with one symbol per unit, aligned in rows
Two bars aligned to show the difference for 'how many more'
Frequency table as the source the graph is drawn from
authoredAnswer: Interpreting: reads both bars against the scale and gives the DIFFERENCE (e.g. cats 9 − dogs 6 = 3), explaining the comparison. Translating: draws a fish bar to 4 and a birds bar to 2, equal width, rising from the baseline, correctly against the scale.

wrongAnswers.revealedBy: Child gives the cats value (9) rather than 9 − 6 = 3
wrongAnswers.fix: Align the two bars and count the squares the taller one sticks up by; name 'how many more' as that gap, then re-ask

wrongAnswers.revealedBy: Child's read value is consistently one out, or they count lines including the baseline
wrongAnswers.fix: Track the bar top straight across to the scale number; check bars start at zero — a reading lapse to steady

wrongAnswers.revealedBy: New bars don't start at the baseline, differ in width, or the picture-graph symbols vary in size
wrongAnswers.fix: Re-establish the grammar: equal-width bars from a common baseline, one square per unit; connect back to one unit = one item

before.name: Sorting Data into Categories
before.reason: Drawing picture/bar graphs extends organising and representing data
